rules: P2 DECISION-AUTHORITY.md §3 A1-A9 with the §5 v0.2 changes C1-C5

decisions.statement: Add a pure state transition Commands.move (appointment id, today, date, time, state) in src/Clinic/Commands.fs and a `move <appointment> <date> <time>` case in Cli.dispatch that parses the date and time with the existing Commands.parseDate/parseTime, exactly as `book` does. On success the output is `<id> moved to <yyyy-MM-dd> at <HH:mm>` using the existing Commands.date/Commands.time formatters. No new rule is written in Commands or Cli (docs/architecture.md).
reasons: A2 'docs/architecture.md' does not resolve to a requirement, decision record or approval

decisions.statement: A move keeps the appointment's id, patient and clinician and changes only its date and time. It is checked with the same rule functions booking uses, in booking's order: Rules.withinBookingHorizon (DEC-C01) then Rules.slotFree (DEC-C02) for the appointment's own clinician, evaluated against the current state, returning the same ClinicError (OutsideBookingHorizon / SlotTaken) and therefore the same error text. The booking checks that cannot apply to an existing appointment (unknown patient, unknown clinician, appointment id already exists) are not applied. A refused move returns Error and leaves the state unchanged.

An unknown appointment id is refused with the existing UnknownAppointment error, printing `error: unknown appointment <id>`, and changes nothing. Error order follows `book`: an invalid date or time word is reported first (parsed in Cli before the command runs, as for book), then unknown appointment, then booking horizon, then slot taken. This order is taken from how booking already behaves, not newly invented; if the owner wants a different order it is an open question.

Moving an appointment to the date and time it already occupies is treated literally under R1: a new booking for that clinician at that slot would be refused because the slot is taken (by this appointment), so the move is refused with `error: <clinician> is already booked on <date> at <time>` and changes nothing. The slot check does not exclude the appointment being moved. UNRESOLVED QUESTION for Clinical Operations: should a move to the same slot (or the appointment's own slot) instead be accepted as a no-op? Not implemented unless authorized.

Because R1 requires a move to be refused exactly when a new booking would be, move calls the existing Rules.slotFree unchanged and so behaves like booking for every clinician, including the existing hard-coded walk-in behaviour for k2 (Dr. Patel) whose slots never count as taken. That k2 behaviour has no decision record in docs/decisions/ or approval in docs/approvals/; this work neither relies on it as authorized policy nor changes or removes it (existing behaviour must keep working). UNRESOLVED QUESTION for Clinical Operations: is the k2 walk-in exception in Rules.slotFree an accepted rule, and should it apply to moves?

Insert `move <appointment> <date> <time>` into Cli.usage directly after `cancel <appointment>`, so `help` lists it there and a `move` line with the wrong number of words gets the existing `error: usage: move <appointment> <date> <time>` treatment. Update the command list in README.md#Commands to match (documentation only).

Add tests in tests/Clinic.Tests/Acceptance/ for criteria the provided acceptance tests do not cover: a refused move (slot taken, outside horizon, unknown appointment) leaves the schedule unchanged; the old slot is freed after a successful move; moving keeps the patient and clinician. The provided acceptance tests are not modified. `dotnet test Clinic.slnx` must pass.
